name: Lençóis Maranhenses
tagline: A landscape of rolling white sand dunes filled with turquoise rainwater lagoons, like bedsheets thrown across the coast, at its most spectacular in the middle of the year.
highlight: Wading through a warm, clear lagoon between dunes at sunset, with not another person in sight.
shortDescription: A national park of about 1,500 square kilometres of dunes and seasonal lagoons on Brazil's north coast, explored from Barreirinhas and Santo Amaro by 4x4, boat and on foot.
metaDescription: A Lençóis Maranhenses travel guide: dunes and lagoons, Barreirinhas, Santo Amaro, Atins, the Preguiças River, best time to see the lagoons, how to get there from São Luís and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: São Luís (SLZ), about 260 km, or Barreirinhas (BRB) small airport
knownFor: White dunes, turquoise lagoons, remote scenery, kitesurfing

image.file: File:Parque Nacional dos Lençóis Maranhenses Paulo Cattelan (03).jpg
image.alt: White sand dunes and blue lagoons in the Lençóis Maranhenses National Park

intro: The Lençóis Maranhenses National Park is a strip of coastline in the state of Maranhão, about 70 km long and 50 km deep, where huge white sand dunes roll inland from the Atlantic. The name means the bedsheets of Maranhão, from the way the dunes look like sheets spread across the land. It is not a desert, since the region receives heavy rain from January to June, and the water collects in hollows between the dunes, forming thousands of lagoons that can be several metres deep.

The lagoons are at their fullest from about June to September, when the water is a striking blue or green against white sand, and in the dry months from November to January many dry out. The dunes are made of quartz sand blown from the coast, and they move each year with the wind. Fish arrive in the lagoons from the rivers and the sea, and survive the dry season buried in the mud as eggs.

The park is remote and uncrowded. Most visitors base themselves at Barreirinhas, the gateway town, or at small villages such as Santo Amaro and Atins, and explore the dunes on 4x4 tours or on foot. It is a landscape that photographs superbly, and a good addition to a longer trip in north-east Brazil.

whyVisit.intro: Lençóis Maranhenses is a uniquely beautiful landscape, and one of the great natural wonders of Brazil.

points.title: Dunes and lagoons
points.text: Wave after wave of white sand with clear lagoons between them.

points.title: Swimming in the dunes
points.text: The lagoons are safe and warm, ideal for a swim.

points.title: Remote and quiet
points.text: Far from large crowds and cities.

points.title: River and coast
points.text: Boat trips on the Preguiças River and the Atlantic coast.

attractionsIntro: There are several entry points to the park, each with a different style of visit.

attractions.name: Lagoa Azul and Lagoa Bonita

image.file: File:Parque Nacional dos Lencois Maranhenses Filo Vasconcellos (24).jpg
image.alt: A blue lagoon among white sand dunes in Lençóis Maranhenses National Park

attractions.text: Two of the best-known lagoons, near Barreirinhas, reached by 4x4 and a short walk through the dunes.
attractions.tip: Go at sunset for the light and cooler temperatures.

attractions.name: Santo Amaro do Maranhão
attractions.text: A small village on the eastern edge of the dunes, with lagoons that can be reached on foot from the village, and a quiet atmosphere.
attractions.tip: A good base for multi-day treks.

attractions.name: Rio Preguiças boat trip

image.alt: A boat on the Rio Preguiças with dunes and mangroves at Barreirinhas

attractions.text: A river trip from Barreirinhas past mangroves, dunes, the fishing village of Mandacaru and the Vassouras dunes, ending at the lighthouse.

attractions.name: Atins
attractions.text: A remote beach village at the river mouth, with kitesurfing, fresh fish and quiet dunes right at the coast.

attractions.name: The dunes at sunset

image.file: File:Casal de turistas caminha em uma duna, enquanto o dia morre nos Lençóis Maranhenses (edited).jpg
image.alt: Two tourists walking on a dune at sunset in Lençóis Maranhenses

attractions.text: The dunes change colour as the sun sets, and the lagoons reflect the sky. It is the most popular time for tours.
attractions.tip: Bring a flashlight for the walk back.

thingsToDoIntro: Tours and guides are the main way to see the dunes.

thingsToDo.title: Swim in a lagoon
thingsToDo.text: Wade and swim in warm, clear water, in the middle of the dunes.

thingsToDo.title: Take a 4x4 tour to the dunes
thingsToDo.text: A bumpy ride to the lagoons, with time to walk and swim.

thingsToDo.title: Do a multi-day trek
thingsToDo.text: The Travessia is a walk across the dunes from Atins to Santo Amaro, with overnight stays in villages.

thingsToDo.title: Ride down the Preguiças River
thingsToDo.text: See mangroves, monkeys and dunes from a boat.
thingsToDo.tip: Book a half- or full-day trip.

thingsToDo.title: Try kitesurfing at Atins
thingsToDo.text: Strong, steady winds make the coast a kite destination.

thingsToDo.title: Fly over the dunes
thingsToDo.text: A small-plane flight gives a view of the lagoons.

foodIntro: Maranhão's food is fish- and shellfish-based, with regional specialities.

foods.name: Arroz de cuxá
foods.text: Rice with a paste of roasted sesame seeds, sorrel and dried shrimp, a Maranhão speciality.

foods.name: Fresh fish and shrimp
foods.text: Grilled or fried, with rice and beans.

foods.name: Juçara açaí
foods.text: Local açaí, eaten as a thick bowl.

accommodation.intro: Stay in Barreirinhas or in villages near the park.

areas.name: Santo Amaro
areas.text: Small guesthouses close to the dunes.

gettingThere.intro: Barreirinhas is about 260 km east of São Luís, the state capital.

options.text: Direct flights from Brasília, São Paulo, Rio and other cities.
Vans and buses run from São Luís to Barreirinhas, about 3 to 4 hours.
A popular route by 4x4 and boat, called the Rota das Emoções.

gettingAround.intro: Tours are the main way to move, since the park is roadless.

options.text: Vehicles run from Barreirinhas to the dunes.
Walking in the dunes is the best way to see the lagoons.

bestTime.headline: June–September
bestTime.summary: The rainy season from January to June fills the lagoons, which are at their fullest between June and September, and start to dry from October.

seasons.text: Rain fills the lagoons, but skies can be cloudy.
Lagoons full, skies clear and days sunny.
Lagoons shrink, with hot, windy weather.

bestTime.avoid: November to January, when most lagoons have dried up.

itinerary.title: Three days in Lençóis Maranhenses
itinerary.intro: A dune tour, a river trip and a day for the coast.

days.title: The dunes
days.afternoon: A 4x4 tour to Lagoa Azul and Lagoa Bonita.

days.title: River and coast
days.morning: A boat trip to Atins and Vassouras.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you get the best from the dunes.
tips: Visit from June to September for full lagoons.
Take a hat, sunscreen and water, since there is no shade.
Go at sunset for cooler temperatures.
Book a reputable tour and guide.
Do not leave litter, and stay on marked areas.

faq.a: From about June to September, after the rainy season.

faq.q: How many days do you need?
faq.a: Three days is enough for the dunes, river and coast.
No. It receives heavy rain, which fills the lagoons.

faq.q: Can I swim in the lagoons?
faq.a: Yes. They are safe, warm and clear.
Fly to São Luís, then take a van or car to Barreirinhas, about 3 to 4 hours.

faq.q: Can I visit without a tour?
faq.a: Most areas require a tour or guide, since the dunes are confusing.
